headline: Highest risk is data leakage: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can expose financial data, while LightZero has no filesystem/network access, making other pairwise risks mostly low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no input surfaces or file/network access, so it cannot ingest OpenBBTerminal output by default. OpenBBTerminal can expose MCP/REST/FastAPI interfaces, but without a bridge into LightZero there is no plausible prompt-injection pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies OpenBBTerminal output into a LightZero prompt or file, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard or shared filesystem is introduced, reassess the pathway.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe OpenBBTerminal output into LightZero prompts.
Use explicit human review before any manual copy-paste bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared orchestrator is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces, so leakage risk exists if those outputs are shared. LightZero is local-only with no filesystem or network access, so it is not a direct exfiltration path; the pair’s risk is limited unless an operator bridges data into OpenBBTerminal.
conditions: IF financial or licensed data from OpenBBTerminal is copied into another system, leakage risk increases.
IF a shared workspace is added, reassess for cross-agent exposure.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive financial data in shared folders.
Restrict OpenBBTerminal API access to trusted localhost clients.
Review any exported reports before sharing externally.
requires-engineering: add access controls and audit logs to shared data paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot conflict over mutable resources with OpenBBTerminal. OpenBBTerminal also lacks filesystem write and git modification, so there is no overlapping write surface to contend over.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, reassess for conflicts.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, locking becomes necessary.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same environment.
Do not mount a shared writable repository.
Run separate instances with separate working directories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can produce financial outputs, but LightZero has no ingestion or action-taking path, so there is no default cascade from one agent’s output into the other’s decisions. The pair lacks a documented verification chain or downstream authority, making cascading error unlikely without an external orchestrator.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds OpenBBTerminal outputs into LightZero as authoritative inputs, cascade risk rises.
IF LightZero is used to automate actions based on OpenBBTerminal outputs, reassess.
mitigations: Require human review of OpenBBTerminal outputs.
Do not automate decisions from one agent into the other.
Keep the agents in separate workflows.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data and exposes API/MCP surfaces, so compliance obligations around retention, licensing, and access control are plausible. LightZero is not a compliance driver here because it touches no data classes and has no network or filesystem access; the main concern is OpenBBTerminal’s handling of regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through OpenBBTerminal, retention and access controls must be verified.
IF licensed data is exported from OpenBBTerminal, license terms must be checked before redistribution.
mitigations: Confirm data-retention settings in OpenBBTerminal.
Limit access to licensed datasets.
Review export destinations before sharing.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for financial data.
